title: AI Capex and Bubble Fears (Meta, Alphabet, Anthropic IPO, Shiller P/E)
summary: Gotrade News - Anthropic's IPO has no date or price range yet: the AI lab filed its S-1 on Oct. 26 to list on the Nasdaq as ANT, the company said . CNBC
body_markdown:
## What Is Anthropic Worth?


Anthropic has not disclosed an IPO valuation, and its share count and price range are not yet determined, according to the company.[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/anthropic-ipo-live-updates-ai-s-1-filing.html) reported that its May 2026 funding round raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation.


The prospectus shows revenue of $16.29 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2026, up 1,304% from $1.16 billion a year earlier, as reported by CNBC. The net loss reached $80.7 billion, of which about $72 billion came from accounting charges tied to changes in the value of convertible notes.


Anthropic also disclosed about $417 billion in future payments to compute providers, plus $125 billion to $150 billion more for capacity delivered from 2028 to 2031.


Wharton professor David Hsu told CNBC "It's a great technology," while questioning how it translates into a viable business.


## Where Will Anthropic Stock Trade?


Anthropic plans to list its Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley named as underwriters, according to[its S-1 announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/s1-sec) .


Two of its backers already trade publicly: per[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/26/anthropic-ipo-live-updates-ai-s-1-filing.html) , Amazon has invested $13 billion since 2023, with its stake capped at 12% and its shares nonvoting, while Google holds an option to buy up to $10 billion of Class N stock at the IPO price.


The same companies supply much of its computing power. CNBC tallied $110 billion of commitments on Amazon's Trainium chips through 2036 and $114.5 billion on Google's TPUs through 2033, alongside at least $44.9 billion with Microsoft.


## Big Tech 2026 Capex Guidance After Q3 Earnings


Days after the prospectus landed, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon reported quarterly results that added to investor worries about AI infrastructure spending, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/anthropic-ipo-ai-spending.html) . The table below compiles 2026 capex guidance from[Meta's Oct. 21 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001326801/000162828026066700/meta-09302026xexhibit991.htm) and CNBC's Oct. 31 report.


Company 2026 capex guidance Latest change


Meta Platforms $135 billion to $145 billion, including finance-lease principal Range narrowed from $130 billion to $145 billion


Alphabet Up to $205 billion Guidance kept


Amazon About $220 billion Reiterated


Microsoft $170 billion Lowered from $175 billion


Alphabet reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion, and[its shares fell almost 13% on Thursday, Oct. 29](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/google-googl-stock-news-october-30-2026/) , their worst day ever, per CNBC.[Amazon's third-quarter report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/amazon-amzn-stock-news-november-2-2026/) showed a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow, an outflow of $42.4 billion over the trailing 12 months, while Microsoft kept positive free cash flow of $18.6 billion and announced a $25 billion bond offering.


## S&P Shifts Meta (META) Outlook to Negative


According to[Meta's earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001326801/000162828026066700/meta-09302026xexhibit991.htm) , third-quarter capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, reached $34.91 billion, leaving free cash flow at negative $2.12 billion. Meta has not given a 2027 figure, but said it expects to keep investing aggressively in its core business and AI initiatives.


S&P Global Ratings revised the outlook on Meta's AA- rating to negative from stable on Oct. 30, as reported by[The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/meta-sp-outlook-negative-ai-spending) . The agency expects leverage to rise above 1.0x as soon as 2027, from about 0.1x last year, which would breach the limit for the current rating, and said Meta's ability to monetize its AI investments is "more limited than that of its peers."


The Next Web noted that, unlike Amazon, Microsoft and Google, Meta has no cloud business that rents out computing power. Meta spokesperson Kamran Mumtaz said, "We respectfully disagree with S&P's assertion about Meta's AI monetization capabilities," adding that the company sees "significant product and business opportunities ahead of us, supporting our very strong credit profile."


## Shiller CAPE at 40.13, Near Its December 1999 Peak


The S&P 500's cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings ratio, which compares prices with 10 years of inflation-adjusted earnings, closed at 40.13 on Friday, Oct. 30, according to[Multpl](https://www.multpl.com/shiller-pe) . That sits below the record of 44.19 set in December 1999 but far above the long-run mean of 17.44.


Tech stocks slid the same day. The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9% on Friday, its first three-week losing streak since March, as Nvidia and other chip stocks declined after Intel issued a weak forecast, CNBC reported.


BTIG managing director Jonathan Krinsky described the tech earnings fallout as "The Techsas Chainsaw Massacre," and The Next Web reported the Nasdaq 100 fell 3.5% over the week, briefly entering correction territory.
